points.text: Anyone whose constitutionally protected rights or legally protected interests are harmed may seek legal remedies.

'Other groups' in the provision means bodies other than natural persons and legal persons that lack legal capacity. The purpose is to protect, within limits, such a group's personality rights and property interests.

To uphold constitutional protection of personality and property rights, a group without legal capacity is protected if it has a set name, organization and independent will, and has used its name in business or activities for years, gaining real public recognition and an interest worth protecting, whether or not it serves the public good.
The rule protects group names from being harmed and also protects consumers, so it does not conflict with Article 22 of the Constitution.

A pending trademark application is not yet a registered right, but the rights arising from it can be transferred, so they have property value and are constitutionally protected property. Its holder may seek legal remedies if they are unlawfully harmed.
Whether a company preparatory office counts as an 'other group' depends on the specific circumstances under this interpretation.

raw.answer: The case asked what the phrase "other necessary measures" means in the Credit Cooperative Act and the Banking Act, which let regulators act against failing cooperatives and banks. The court said it covers only a reasonable measure of last resort, used when the situation is urgent and the measures the laws list would not work. It also set extra conditions for regulators who arrange for a failing bank or cooperative to be taken over by another financial institution.
raw.held: "Other necessary measures" means an unavoidable, reasonable step taken when the listed measures would clearly fail because of urgency, and only if the legal preconditions are met. For a takeover of a failing bank or cooperative by another institution, the failing one must also have been unable to promptly provide enough funds, security or another effective way to cover its shortfall, and the legal takeover procedure must be followed.

points.text: The listed measures in both laws let regulators at each level weigh the actual situation. Following the proportionality principle, they choose the means that protects financial order at the lowest social cost while also protecting people's property rights.

"Necessary measures" apply only when the law's precondition is met: a cooperative that cannot be soundly run and risks harming members and depositors, or a bank whose finances have badly worsened and which cannot pay its debts or risks harming depositors.
Such measures are allowed only when the situation is urgent and even the measures the laws list would not achieve the expected result. They must be an unavoidable, reasonable means.

For a takeover by another institution, the usual conditions must be met. In addition, the failing bank or cooperative must have been unable to promptly offer enough funds, security or another effective way to cover its asset shortfall.
The takeover must also go through the procedure set by the relevant laws and rules to count as a necessary measure.

raw.answer: The case asked whether the Act on Restoring Rights Damaged During the Martial Law Period was unconstitutional in who it covers and on what conditions. The court found that limiting the Act to insurrection and treason cases was constitutional. It found, however, that Article 6 left out people who suffered equal harm, and that this conflicted with the constitution's equality clause (Article 7).
raw.held: Limiting the Act to insurrection and treason cases is within the legislature's discretion and does not violate the constitution. Article 6's omission of people detained or not lawfully released outside the stage before an acquittal becomes final violates Article 7, and those people may claim state compensation under Article 6 within two years of the ruling's announcement.

points.text: Military trials during martial law used different procedures from ordinary criminal cases and gave weaker remedies, so the legislature passed the Act to restore rights or give compensation.

Covering only insurrection and treason was constitutional because these crimes involve political factors, and military courts may have erred in finding facts and applying the law under martial law. Leaving out other criminal cases is within legislative discretion.

Article 6 covered only people detained or punished before a final acquittal. It left out people held or not lawfully released at other stages, such as around a decision not to prosecute, release for insufficient suspicion, after an acquittal, or after a sentence was completed. They suffered equal harm, and nothing in the nature of things justified treating them differently, so this was a serious legislative defect.
Applying Article 6 as written would compensate only those detained before a final acquittal. This would create legal inequality and conflict with Article 7 of the constitution.
So those omitted people may claim state compensation under Article 6, in the same way as the covered group, where their detention or punishment is well founded.
The two-year claim period normally runs from the Act's promulgation date, which raises no constitutional problem. For claims made under this ruling, the two years run from the ruling's announcement.

who: People tried by military courts during martial law for insurrection or treason
People detained or not lawfully released outside the period before a final acquittal
People convicted of other crimes, who are not covered by the Act

raw.answer: The case asked whether a provision of the Business Accounting Act is unconstitutional because it lets the central competent authority approve who may work as a bookkeeper (商業會計記帳人). The court decided that bookkeepers practice a specialized profession, so under Article 86, item 2 of the Constitution their qualification to practice must be set by law through examination and selection. The provision leaving this to the authority's approval conflicts with the Constitution and is not to be applied.
raw.held: The part of Article 5, paragraph 4 of the Business Accounting Act that leaves the central competent authority to approve bookkeepers' qualifications violates Article 86, item 2 of the Constitution and shall not be applied.

points.text: Business accounting work means handling business accounts and preparing financial reports under generally accepted accounting principles, which affects the public interest and people's property rights.
Anyone doing this work as a profession therefore needs a certain level of accounting knowledge and experience.

Bookkeepers were allowed alongside accountants to help small and mid-sized businesses that cannot afford to hire an accountant, but they still need real expertise in bookkeeping and tax accounting so the records are accurate and can be checked by the authority.

Because bookkeepers handle business accounting affairs, they belong to a specialized profession, so their qualification must be obtained by examination or screening under law, as Article 86, item 2 of the Constitution requires.
Leaving bookkeepers' qualification to the authority's approval therefore conflicts with the Constitution and the part is not to be applied.

raw.answer: The case asked whether an Executive Yuan order listing which public jobs count when a retired military officer takes a new post was unconstitutional. The court held that the order was not unconstitutional. It found the order a necessary supplement to the unclear table in the officer service regulations, consistent with the law's purpose and with the constitutional protection of the right to subsist and property rights.
raw.held: The Executive Yuan's 1979 notice on the job categories for retirees who take public posts is a necessary supplement to the regulation's unclear table. It does not go against the legislative purpose or the constitutional protection of the right to subsist and property rights.

points.text: The retirement pension in Article 27's table is meant as care for officers' long service in defending the country. It is not pay for later public jobs, and it does not let retirees draw two salaries from the public purse, which would burden state finances.

So 'public servant' in the table means anyone holding a paid public post, whatever the job title or the amount of pay. This matches the pension-stopping rules in other retirement laws, such as the Civil Service Retirement Act and the school staff retirement regulations.

The Executive Yuan notice sets out job categories such as elected representatives, political appointees, regular and temporary staff, contract staff, and military-unit hired staff. It was a necessary supplement by the competent authority to the unclear table, consistent with the legislative purpose.
The notice does not conflict with the constitutionally protected right to subsist or property rights.

Constitution Articles 85 and 86 (item 1) deal with selecting and examining civil servants and do not define who is one. The court can only review the laws a final judgment applied, not whether the court applied them properly. Whether the petitioners fall under the notice is a factual question for the courts, outside this interpretation.

who: Retirees who take paid public posts

raw.answer: The case asked whether a rule in the implementing regulations of the National Health Insurance Act was unconstitutional. The rule sets the insured amount, which is used to calculate premiums, for self-employed professionals such as accountants, lawyers, architects and doctors. The court decided the rule is not unconstitutional.
raw.held: The regulation sets the insured amount for self-employed professionals, with the highest level of the schedule as the ceiling and the highest level of the labor insurance wage schedule as the floor. The court held that this fits what the Act authorizes and does not violate the constitutional protection of property rights.

points.text: Health insurance premiums are compulsory charges collected to keep the national health insurance system running. They are a kind of public-law money payment with the nature of a contribution (分擔金).

Premium rates must be set by actuarial calculation based on expected loss rates. Benefits and premiums must be balanced, and premiums may go only as far as covering the state's costs of providing benefits.

Because it is social insurance, people with different incomes pay different premiums, which follows ability to pay. Insured amounts are worked out by grouping people into types, which keeps the system simple.
The Act authorizes the competent authority to set a graded schedule of insured amounts, which is the basis for calculating premiums.
Under the Act, self-employed professionals with no fixed income report their own insured amount from the schedule, and the insurer checks it and may adjust it if the report is untrue.

The regulation's upper and lower limits are based on the nature of the insured person's occupation as the Act provides. They fit the Act's authorization and do not go against the protection of property rights.

who: Self-employed professionals such as accountants, lawyers, architects and doctors
Employers with 20 or more insured employees
Insured persons paying health insurance premiums
The health insurance authority and insurer

raw.answer: The case asked whether a Ministry of Finance formula for calculating the income tax reduction under the Investment Incentive Statute was unconstitutional. The formula treats non-operating losses as zero when they exceed non-operating income. The court did not strike the rule down, but said that non-operating losses must be assigned to the right product line where that can be done, or else estimated by a revenue ratio, and that the authorities must revise the rules quickly.
raw.held: The "treat as zero" rule is justified in order to stop non-exempt product income from going untaxed. But related non-operating losses must be assigned directly where that can be done reasonably and clearly, and otherwise estimated by the ratio of exempt-product sales revenue to taxable-product sales revenue, to meet tax fairness. The relevant agencies must revise the rules promptly.

points.text: The Constitution's duty to pay tax according to law covers the taxpayer, tax items, rates, methods and tax reductions. Tax laws must be read by their purpose, economic meaning and fair substantive taxation, and agency interpretations must meet this standard.
The Investment Incentive Statute aimed to encourage investment through tax breaks, and only businesses meeting the set categories and standards get them. This ensures fairness and prevents abuse.

The Ministry's formula was a convenience for tax collection. Treating non-operating losses as zero avoids letting income from non-exempt products escape tax, which matches the statute's purpose of limiting relief to income from the encouraged products.
Non-operating losses come in many kinds, such as interest, exchange losses, and damage to goods or disaster losses. So they should not all be treated the same way.

Losses tied to business items should be assigned directly where that can be done reasonably and clearly. If they are hard to separate, they should be estimated by the ratio of exempt-product revenue to taxable-product revenue, as tax fairness requires.
The relevant agencies must promptly review and revise the related rules in line with this interpretation.

who: Businesses claiming income tax reductions under the investment incentive law
Tax authorities that apply the Ministry of Finance formula
Businesses with both exempt and taxable products

raw.answer: The case asked whether Taiwan's National Health Insurance Act is unconstitutional in forcing people to enroll, pay premiums, and pay late fees. The court held that these rules are consistent with the Constitution, and that also requiring people already in public-servant, labor, or farmer insurance to join does not violate the protection of reliance interests. It added that people unable to pay must be given suitable assistance and not simply denied benefits.
raw.held: The compulsory enrollment, premium payment, and late-fee provisions of the National Health Insurance Act do not conflict with the Constitution, and requiring those already in public, labor, or farmer insurance to join is also acceptable. The state must give suitable help to people who cannot pay premiums and may not simply refuse them benefits, and the relevant agencies must review and improve the system in good time.

points.text: The Constitution and its Additional Articles set the national policy of social insurance, public health care, and national health insurance, so the legislature may make laws for it; how to design the system is up to the legislature's discretion.
Compulsory enrollment and premium payment rest on social mutual aid, risk sharing, and the public interest, and are needed for the state to meet its duty to provide health care to all citizens.
The late fee is a necessary and reasonable means of getting insurers and insured persons to pay what they owe, and it does not go beyond the limit set by Article 23 of the Constitution.
People who cannot pay premiums must receive suitable state assistance and may not simply be refused benefits, in line with the constitutional aim of protecting those unable to support themselves.
Making those already in public, labor, or farmer insurance also join serves to unify medical benefits into one fair national system and to allocate medical resources reasonably.

Because the conditions of this compulsory social insurance are set by law for everyone, unlike a voluntary insurance contract, changing them does not violate the protection of reliance interests; the agencies must still review the system in good time.

who: People required to enroll in national health insurance
Public servants, workers, and farmers already in other insurance

raw.answer: The case asked how the President should nominate and appoint the Judicial Yuan's President, Vice President and Grand Justices before 2003, when the constitutional amendments were changing. The court held that the 1994 amendment, Article 4, applies if a vacancy disrupts the Judicial Yuan's work before then. It also said the 1997 amendment left this gap by mistake.
raw.held: If the Judicial Yuan's President, Vice President or a current Grand Justice position falls vacant before 2003 and this disrupts the Judicial Yuan's normal work, the President's nomination must follow the procedure in Article 4 of the amendment promulgated on August 1, 1994.

points.text: The 1992 amendment (Article 13, paragraph 1) had the President nominate and the National Assembly approve, and the Control Yuan no longer had the power to consent.
The 1997 amendment (Article 5, paragraph 1) made major changes and is stated to take effect from 2003, so it cannot apply to those nominated before then.
The current President, Grand Justices and the vacant Vice President position were nominated under the 1992 amendment, and the Grand Justices' nine-year terms run to October 2003.
The 1997 amendment says nothing about how to appoint people when a vacancy arises during this transition period.
The Constitution's Article 79 consent by the Control Yuan no longer applies, so it cannot be used for these nominations.
The 1997 amendment should have used a transitional rule drawing on the 1994 Article 4; leaving it out was a drafting mistake, so that procedure applies.

who: Judicial Yuan President and Vice President

raw.answer: The case asked whether a Ministry of Finance letter from 1977 was unconstitutional. The letter said that a producer's income from trading goods it did not make itself, and its non-business income, does not get the tax cap under the Statute for Encouraging Investment. The court decided the letter is not unconstitutional.
raw.held: The 1977 Ministry of Finance letter is consistent with the Statute, did not change the tax-benefit rules or add to producers' tax burden, and does not conflict with the constitutional principle that taxes must be set by law.

points.text: The Statute was meant to encourage investment and speed economic development, mainly through tax reductions.
Because economic needs change over time, the Statute let the Executive Yuan set the encouraged categories and standards, and only producers meeting them can get the tax cap.
The letter was an interpretation by the responsible authority, issued in its own role, to carry out the Statute and the Executive Yuan's standards when working out taxable income.
The letter matches the Statute's aim of limiting tax benefits to income from producers' own production of encouraged products.
The letter did not change the tax-benefit rules set by law or increase producers' tax burden, so it does not conflict with the principle that taxes must be set by law.

who: Producers that also trade goods they did not make
Ministry of Finance as tax authority

raw.answer: The case asked whether rules in the civil service appointment and pay laws on 'high-rank, low-post' staff (officials transferred to a lower-ranked post) are unconstitutional. The court found that these rules, in the way they work, have an effect similar to a demotion or pay cut, and that this does not fully fit the constitutional protection of the right to hold public office. It told the responsible authority to review and amend the rules promptly.
raw.held: The court held that transferring an official to a lower grade, where their pay level is already at the top of the new grade's scale and they can never be advanced, in practice acts like a disciplinary demotion or pay cut and does not fully match the constitutional protection of the right to hold public office. The responsible authority must promptly review and amend the Civil Service Appointment Act, the Civil Service Pay Act and related regulations.

points.text: The Constitution guarantees the right to hold public office. An official's rank and pay level, once lawfully fixed, cannot be lowered unless the disciplinary body decides so through the legal procedure. This is an institutional protection.

The Appointment Act lets a superior transfer a higher-grade official to a lower rank or grade, but once transferred, the Pay Act and its enforcement rules bar further advancement in pay at evaluation if the official is already at the top pay level of the new grade.
Such officials get no chance of advancement however hard they work or however good their results, and this applies whether or not their original grade had reached its top pay level.

So although the transfer is not called a demotion or pay cut, it in practice has a similar disciplinary effect, which does not fully fit the constitutional protection. The authority must therefore promptly review and amend the laws and related rules.

who: Civil servants transferred to lower-ranked posts
Officials whose pay is at the top of their new grade
Authorities responsible for appointment and pay rules
